title: Sum-over-poles framework for quantum embedding to approach the real-frequency axis
authors: Alessandro Carbone, Massimo Capone, Nicola Marzari, Tommaso Chiarotti
abstract: We introduce a real-frequency framework for the quantum embedding of solids, based on sum-over-poles (SOP) representations. We partition the lattice into periodically repeated interacting fragments and derive an embedded Dyson equation for the fragment, to be solved self-consistently. The resulting scheme generalizes the algorithmic-inversion method of our previous work to interacting Hamiltonians and is closely related to dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), especially when an extended impurity problem is introduced. By exploiting the compact pole expansion of the embedding potential, we carry out the self-consistent procedure close to the real axis, which avoids ill-posed analytic continuation. In addition, the SOP representation allows us to introduce a pole-and-residue dynamics, which we use to reach the self-consistent solution. After deriving the method, we benchmark it against exact-diagonalization implementations of DMFT on the one-dimensional Hubbard ring at half filling. The framework offers a natural route to real-space dynamical quantum embedding, for periodic systems as well as for strongly correlated defects in materials.
summary: This paper introduces a novel Sum-over-Poles (SOP) framework for quantum embedding, enabling the study of strongly correlated solids directly on the real-frequency axis. By solving an embedded Dyson equation self-consistently, it overcomes the numerical challenges of analytic continuation. The method is validated against established DMFT results on the 1D Hubbard model, providing a powerful tool for real-space quantum simulation.
main_problem: Developing a real-frequency framework for the quantum embedding of solids to accurately approach the real-frequency axis while avoiding ill-posed analytic continuation issues.
main_result: The Sum-over-Poles (SOP) framework successfully generalizes quantum embedding methods to interacting Hamiltonians, reproducing benchmark results from DMFT on the 1D Hubbard model.
method: The authors use the SOP representation to define the embedding potential and solve the embedded Dyson equation self-consistently, allowing calculations directly on the real-frequency axis.
model_or_system: The framework applies to interacting electrons in a solid lattice, modeled by partitioning the system into interacting fragments. Benchmarking is performed on the one-dimensional Hubbard ring at half-filling.
key_observables: The system Green's function G(omega) and the local Green's function G_loc(omega), particularly their imaginary parts on the real-frequency axis.
important_parameters: Interaction strength U/t (e.g., 1, 4, 7); the number of poles M; and the broadening parameter eta/t.
main_assumptions: The method relies on the block-diagonal approximation for the self-energy and assumes the equivalence between the lattice and an auxiliary system description.
figures_summary: Figures compare the imaginary part of the local Green's function on the imaginary axis versus the real-frequency 'erf' axis, and illustrate the convergence of the self-consistent solution using pole and residue dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the embedded Dyson equation, details the use of the SOP representation to solve it self-consistently, and validates the procedure by benchmarking against exact-diagonalization results for the 1D Hubbard model.
why_interesting: The development of robust real-frequency techniques for strongly correlated systems is crucial for connecting theoretical calculations to measurable spectroscopic quantities, which is highly relevant for AMO and open quantum systems.

FIG. 4: Comparison of the ”pole and residue” dynamics methodology against the reference results of Sec. III A for the half-filled Hubbard ring simulation at M = 6, 8 and U/t = 7 on the erf axis with η = 1. In (a) and (c) we show the evolution (trajectory) of the parameters of the SOP representation using the ratio of each residue/pole with the reference—σk/σRef, and Γk/ΓRef—at M = 6, 8, respectively. As at half filling the poles and residues are symmetric we show the ones pertaining to the positive axis. In (b) and (d) the converged local Green’s functions Gloc are analytically continued to the complex axis ω −i0.2 and compared with the reference.
